overview.name: Link Operations
overview.summary: A controlled URL-shortener prototype with URL lifecycle management, redirects, bounded analytics, idempotent creation, audit events, and reviewer evidence.
overview.architecture: Angular standalone SPA and Spring Boot modular monolith backed by MySQL and Flyway.
overview.runtime: Java 21, Spring Boot 3.5.16, Angular 19.2.25, Node 20, MySQL 8.4.
overview.evidenceBoundary: Repository evidence and observed local validation only; no production use, approval, scale, or performance is claimed.

architecture.name: Angular SPA
architecture.responsibility: Typed management, analytics, review, readiness, and optional portfolio experiences.
architecture.flow: Browser -> same-origin /api and /r paths; reviewer content -> packaged allowlisted JSON.

architecture.name: Spring Boot modular monolith
architecture.responsibility: URL, redirect, analytics, audit, idempotency, rate-limit, and shared operational modules.
architecture.flow: Controllers -> application services -> Spring Data repositories -> MySQL.

architecture.name: MySQL + Flyway
architecture.responsibility: Authoritative URL, click-event, idempotency, and audit persistence with forward-only V1-V4 migrations.
architecture.flow: Flyway migrates before JPA validates; application uses a bounded Hikari connection pool.

architecture.name: Optional local cache
architecture.responsibility: Short-lived in-process redirect lookup acceleration; disabled by default.
architecture.flow: Cache-aside lookup with database fallback; no Redis or distributed invalidation is claimed.

Search, filter, sort, and page non-deleted URLs.
Read URL details and a strong ETag.
Enable a URL with optimistic concurrency.
Disable a URL with optimistic concurrency.
Soft-delete a URL with optimistic concurrency.
Resolve an active, unexpired code without exposing management data.
Return hourly or daily UTC buckets.
Serve a packaged, allowlisted review snapshot; not a filesystem API.
Serve generated relative names from bounded repository roots.
Return sanitized aggregate application health without component details.
Expose controlled prototype metrics; protect or disable before public deployment.

database.purpose: URL identity, destination, code, lifecycle, expiration, and optimistic version.
Minimal best-effort analytics events without raw IP storage.
Request fingerprint and replay outcome for bounded create retries.
Sanitized lifecycle event metadata without destination URLs.

scenarios.name: Greenfield
scenarios.decision: Start with a modular monolith and a thin vertical slice before optional distribution.
scenarios.constraints: Java/Spring/Angular/MySQL, bounded scope, human gates, no invented scale.
scenarios.outcome: Implemented core URL, redirect, analytics, testing, and evidence layers.
scenarios.risk: Scope growth and premature optimization remain open risks.

scenarios.name: Brownfield
scenarios.decision: Add idempotent URL creation as a backward-compatible change.
scenarios.constraints: Existing clients remain valid; optional header; atomic persistence; expiry cleanup.
scenarios.outcome: Fingerprint, replay, conflict, migration, HTTP, and service coverage were added.
scenarios.risk: Docker-backed concurrency and rollback cases remain skipped.

scenarios.name: Ambiguous
scenarios.decision: Interpret production-ready as production-conscious evidence, not production approval.
scenarios.constraints: Unknown identity, moderation, SLO, traffic, retention, and deployment environment.
scenarios.outcome: Assumptions and blockers are explicit instead of silently invented.
scenarios.risk: Human product, security, privacy, and operations decisions remain pending.

scenarios.name: Comparison
scenarios.decision: Use the same evidence discipline while changing the engineering move by context.
scenarios.constraints: Greenfield optimizes sequencing, brownfield compatibility, ambiguous work reversible decisions.
scenarios.outcome: Traceability connects intent, implementation, tests, residual risk, and approval state.
scenarios.risk: Repository has no Git history, so provenance is artifact-based rather than commit-based.

accepted: Bounded modular-monolith implementation and typed Angular feature slices.
Risk-based backend, frontend, API, accessibility, responsive, and real-stack tests.
Sanitized build-time reviewer metadata and explicit honesty markers.
edited: Generated recommendations were reconciled against actual controllers, migrations, tests, and quality evidence.
Security and readiness language was tightened to preserve blockers and pending approvals.
rejected: Redis and distributed infrastructure without measured need.
Forced dependency updates without compatibility review or current supporting findings.
Fabricated portfolio entries, approvals, performance results, or production claims.
excluded: Secrets, credentials, environment dumps, proprietary employer content, and unrestricted filesystem access.
Private chain-of-thought or fabricated AI chat transcripts.

Contradictory dependency-audit output and residual security-risk disposition.
Authentication, moderation, operations, privacy, and public-deployment decisions.

risks.title: Open redirect and phishing abuse
risks.mitigation: Controlled environment, scheme validation, rate limits, future moderation.
risks.residual: No reputation, takedown, or abuse operation exists.

risks.title: Single MySQL dependency
risks.mitigation: Bounded pools/timeouts, safe errors, aggregate health.
risks.residual: No replica, failover, or tested recovery.

risks.title: Dependency and supply-chain findings
risks.mitigation: Pinned lockfiles, minimal dependencies, repeatable audits, and conservative status handling.
risks.residual: Clean npm ci reports 29 findings while immediate explicit audits report zero; current evidence is contradictory and remains FAIL.

risks.title: Migration and recovery failure
risks.mitigation: Forward-only Flyway migrations and clean-schema validation.
risks.residual: Backup/restore and upgrade-path rehearsal are absent.

risks.title: Confidentiality or filesystem exposure
risks.mitigation: Allowlisted generated metadata, fixed assets, empty portfolio.
risks.residual: Future generic viewers or unreviewed content could reopen exposure.

decisions.title: Short-code strategy
decisions.summary: Random base62 codes with unique constraint and bounded retries.
decisions.tradeoff: Simple and horizontally generatable; collisions require retry handling.

decisions.title: MySQL source of truth
decisions.summary: Relational constraints, UTC timestamps, and Flyway ownership.
decisions.tradeoff: Strong fit for lifecycle consistency; creates a critical database dependency.

decisions.title: Best-effort analytics
decisions.summary: Redirect success is isolated from analytics failure.
decisions.tradeoff: Availability wins over complete click accounting.

decisions.title: Optional local cache
decisions.summary: Disabled-by-default in-memory cache rather than baseline Redis.
decisions.tradeoff: Low complexity; no shared cache or global invalidation.

decisions.title: Privacy-minimized analytics
decisions.summary: No raw IP persistence; coarse device and sanitized referrer derivation.
decisions.tradeoff: Reduced privacy exposure; no unique-user or geography claims.

decisions.title: Build-time project display
decisions.summary: Fixed static metadata assets generated from allowlisted repository paths.
decisions.tradeoff: Safe and deployable; not a live repository browser.

limitations: Management and analytics APIs are unauthenticated; public exposure is blocked.
No moderation, reputation, takedown, or abuse-operations workflow exists.
Current npm advisory output is contradictory, and container/base-image plus dedicated backend vulnerability scans are NOT_RUN.
Nineteen Docker/Testcontainers JUnit cases were skipped in the latest local backend run.
No tested backup/restore, failover, disaster recovery, SLO, capacity, load, soak, or chaos evidence exists.
Browser evidence is Chrome-only; manual screen-reader and cross-browser validation are NOT_RUN.
All human approval gates remain PENDING.

readiness.databaseEvidence: MySQL 8.4.10 with Flyway V1-V4 passed nine prior real-stack browser flows; current live DB component detail is intentionally not exposed.
